title: Regional Micro-Model Prospector & Replication Cost Probe
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight operational playbook and signal pipeline to detect small, regional open-model entrants ("micro-models") and estimate the engineering and infra effort to replicate their inference economics in-house or via Dedicated.

Hypothesis: Emerging micro-models (narrow-domain variants released outside major hubs) will appear with localized latency advantages or lower per-token costs. If detected early, Redwood can (1) preemptively benchmark and add fallbacks, (2) negotiate model-sourcing partnerships, or (3) estimate the true replication cost to determine whether to onboard or block.

Success metrics (30d & 90d):
- 30d: pipeline ingesting 8+ candidate micro-model signals/week from artifact feeds (model repos, community forums, vendor announcements).
- 90d: for 6 prioritized candidates produce a replication-cost delta estimate (in $/1M tokens) and a qualitative risk score (latency, license friction, quantization compatibility).

Scope and deliverables:
- Signal sources: GitHub (new model repos), Hugging Face releases (region tags), vendor mailing lists, community Discords, and job postings mentioning model owners.
- Lightweight scraper and metadata normalizer (metadata: size, architecture, pretraining corpus cue, quantization-friendly tags).
- Automated quick-bench harness: run small perf/latency/throughput tests against hosted samples (where allowed) or simulated workloads using model-card heuristics.
- Replication-cost estimator: formula combining GPU type affinity, estimated FP/INT quantization path, token throughput, and engineering effort multiplier (low/med/high).
- Playbook doc: triage matrix and recommended action (monitor, benchmark, onboard, or ignore).

Out of scope: full enterprise onboarding, procurement negotiations, or SLA provision for candidates in this ticket. This ticket only produces cost/risk outputs and the triage playbook prototype.
milestones: 2025-01-20: finalize signal list and initial heuristics
2025-02-05: MVP scraper + normalizer deployed to staging
deliverables: replication-cost estimator spreadsheet + baseline GPU mappings
approach:
Phase 1: reconnaissance (2 weeks) — enumerate top-of-funnel sources, prioritize region filters (APAC, LATAM, EU-local), and prototype a URL-based scraper. Phase 2: lightweight instrumentation (3 weeks) — build normalizer and quick-bench harness using cached model-cards or small sample bundles; get SRE signoff for limited external probe runs. Phase 3: analysis and playbook (1 week) — standardize replication-cost model, publish playbook, and present to GTM and SRE.

Key signals and heuristics: model repo star growth velocity, presence of 'quantized' or 'int8' tags, model-card inference instructions, sample prompts demonstrating latency optimizations, and regional domain names/maintainer handles.

Data governance: we will only scrape publicly available metadata and follow robots.txt; any binary downloads require legal review before automated retrieval.

risks: Legal: ambiguous licenses for some community forks could block downloading artifacts
Signal noise: many forks will be low-quality and create false positives
Estimation variance: replication-cost estimator depends on unknown quantization paths and 3rd-party kernel maturity
